A longer `delay` keeps a page of links from flashing cards at every pointer movement. ```tsx … ``` ## When to use - A preview of what a link leads to: a profile, a repository, a document — enough to decide whether to click. - Context that helps a name make sense — the person behind an `@handle`, the project behind a package. - A short panel with one or two actions that should not interrupt the page. ## When not to use - A label for an icon. Use `tooltip`: it is smaller, quicker, and announced as a description. - Content the user opened on purpose. Use `popover`: hover cards close when the pointer moves on, and anything with a task in it deserves a deliberate open. - Information the user needs to answer a question. Nothing that appears and disappears on hover can be the only place it lives. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `HoverCard` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `delay`, `closeDelay` | Base UI root; `delay` is per card. | | `HoverCardTrigger` | native props, `render` | The link or button the card describes. | | `HoverCardContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, and popup. `side` defaults to `bottom`, `sideOffset` to `4`, `alignOffset` to `4`. | The portal renders `data-slot="hover-card-portal"`; the popup is `data-slot="hover-card-content"`. There is no `HoverCardArrow`: upstream's Base UI surface has none, and the card is a surface rather than a pointer. ## Motion contract | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes | | exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes | | reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – | Same anchored motion as `popover` and `tooltip`: the scale starts at `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the trigger. Hover cards close when the pointer leaves, so the exit has to be short; `fast` is the anchored-surface duration the three share. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the card; moving focus into it keeps it open. | | Escape | Closes the card and returns focus to the trigger. | | Enter / Space | Follows the trigger link, or activates a control inside the card. | Keyboard focus opens the card for the same reason it does in a tooltip: without it, the content would exist only for pointer users. ## Accessibility - The trigger carries the accessible name; the card is supplementary. That is why Cadence does not give the popup `role="dialog"` or wire it as the trigger's description: a panel that may hold several paragraphs and a button is neither a name nor a description, and a screen reader reading it on every focus would be noise. - Interactive content inside the card is reachable in order: Tab moves from the trigger into the card's links and buttons, and the card stays open while focus is inside it. - Hover is never the only path: focus opens it too, and Escape closes it, so the card never traps a keyboard user. - If the card is the only place a piece of information exists, it is in the wrong component — move it into the page or into a `popover`. ## Responsive behavior The panel is `w-64` with `p-4`; Base UI flips it to another side and shifts the alignment when the viewport cannot fit it. On touch devices there is no hover: the trigger still opens the card on focus or tap, and the content must not assume a pointer is nearby. ## Performance - Mounted only while open, so a page of links carries no extra popup trees. - Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript animation loop. The card follows the anchor through the positioner, not through React state. ## Notes for AI - Use `hover-card` only for a preview of the linked thing; use `popover` for anything the user opens to act, and `tooltip` for a label. - The trigger must have its own text or `aria-label`; the card is not its name. - Keep the card small: a person, a repository, a document summary, one action. If it needs scrolling, it wants to be a `popover` or a page.
